subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should OpenClaw stop propagating the host path-to-regexp override into managed plugin npm projects, add Express-4-specific validation, or require affected plugin packages to pin their own override?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but each fix shape changes the core/plugin dependency ownership boundary or only improves diagnosis, and AGENTS/VISION treat plugin APIs, dependency overrides, and lockfiles as maintainer-sensitive surfaces.

options.title: Scope host overrides away from plugin-owned deps
options.body: Adjust managed npm project override propagation so OpenClaw security overrides do not replace a plugin package's Express 4-compatible path-to-regexp graph while preserving core Express 5/router resolution.

options.title: Add validator and keep plugin-owned pinning
options.body: Detect Express 4 plugins resolved with path-to-regexp 8.x and fail with an actionable install/startup error while requiring plugin publishers to ship their own override or Express 5 migration.

options.title: Leave ownership fully downstream
options.body: Keep OpenClaw's current host override propagation and rely on affected plugin maintainers, such as camofox-browser, to pin path-to-regexp or migrate Express.

recommendation.title: Scope host overrides away from plugin-owned deps
recommendation.body: Adjust managed npm project override propagation so OpenClaw security overrides do not replace a plugin package's Express 4-compatible path-to-regexp graph while preserving core Express 5/router resolution.

likelyOwner.reason: This login is the strongest current-history owner for managed npm root override propagation and the workspace override surface involved in the decision.
